To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transmittances of an uncooled prism of refractive-index n=2.5 and prism-angle alpha=30 degrees for incident p- (s-) polarized light exhibit an oscillatory behavior as a function of the internal angle of incidence theta when the MD condition (alpha/2) of a transparent optically-isotropic prism is satisfied.

the condition of minimum internal deviation of light by a prism is the condition of maximum transmittance of p-polarization by the uncoated prism and the condition for the prism to be maximally flat for p-polarization.

(1) the transmittance of p-polarization through a transparent prism is oscillatory as a function of the angle of refraction when the prism is operated at and near its minimum-deviation condition; (2) the oscillation is absent for s-polarization; and (3) the magnitude and angular position of the maxima or minima of the p-polarization oscillatory transmittance curve depend on the prism refractive index and prism angle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transmission of light through an uncoated or coated prism and the condition for minimum deviation.
the transmittance properties of an optically isotropic, homogeneous, uncoated prism and a symmetrically coated, optically isotropic homogeneous prism.
the transmission of p- and S-polarized light by a prism and the conditions of minimum deviation and maximum transmittance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the minimum deviation condition for a prism is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for a maximally flat transmitted intensity for the s polarization and a necessary and sufficient condition for the p polarization.
the MD condition is a necessary and sufficient condition for maximum transmittance of p-polarization, and a sufficient condition for maximum s-polarization.
the MD condition is the only condition for the maximum transmittance of p-polarization and the minimum transmittance of s-polarization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MD condition for a prism is not only a condition of maximum transmittance for s-polarized incident light but also a condition of maximum transmission for p-polarized incident radiation when the prism is uncoated and a condition of maximum ellipsometric contrast when the prism is coated.
the MD condition is a special case of the stationary condition of the intensity transmittance of p-polarization.
, when the condition of minimum internal deviation is satisfied, the transmission of p-polarization is maximally flat, whereas s-polarization is not affected.
